bio-hl.topic: IA: conclusion, evaluation and final report

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A strong IA conclusion should…
options: answer the research question using the processed data
list every piece of equipment used
repeat the introduction word for word
include new data not shown earlier
questions.answer: answer the research question using the processed data
questions.hint: Link back to what you set out to find.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is an example of a systematic error?
options: A thermometer that always reads 0.5 °C too high
Slight variation in stopwatch reaction time
Rounding values in the final digit
questions.answer: A thermometer that always reads 0.5 °C too high
questions.hint: Systematic errors push results in the same direction every time.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which type of error can be reduced by repeating trials and calculating a mean?
questions.hint: It is the type that varies unpredictably.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement describes a limitation rather than a simple mistake?
options: The conclusion only applies to the temperature range tested
The student forgot to label one axis
questions.answer: The conclusion only applies to the temperature range tested
questions.hint: Limitations concern how far results can be extended.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Error bars showing standard deviation overlap considerably between two means. This suggests that…
options: the difference between the means may not be significant
questions.answer: the difference between the means may not be significant
questions.hint: Think about how much spread there is in each data set.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Name a statistical test commonly used to compare the means of two independent, normally distributed samples.
questions.hint: Its name is a single letter plus 'test'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A statistical test gives p = 0.03, using a significance level of 0.05. The student should…
questions.hint: Compare p with the significance level.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A trend line has R² = 0.92. This means…
options: the line fits the data closely
the independent variable causes the change
questions.answer: the line fits the data closely

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A pipette measures 25.0 ± 0.5 cm³. What is the percentage uncertainty?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the maximum word count for the IB Biology internal assessment report in the current syllabus?
questions.hint: It is the same limit across the IB sciences.

questions.subject: bio

one variable definitely causes the other

questions.subject: bio

It was a good experiment overall

questions.q: What was the vote of the Supreme Court in Brown v. Board of Education?

questions.q: What phrase from the 1955 ruling (Brown II) on implementing desegregation was criticised for allowing delay?

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: What organisation was formed in 1955 to lead the Montgomery Bus Boycott? (three words)

questions.subject: hist

questions.q: Which court case ended segregation on Montgomery's buses?

To register voters in rural Mississippi

questions.q: Why did images from Birmingham in 1963 increase national support for civil rights?

The campaign was ignored by the media
The city desegregated immediately without protest

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which document did Martin Luther King write while imprisoned in 1963?

The bombing of a Birmingham church
The arrest of the Little Rock Nine

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Evaluate the role of Martin Luther King in the success of the civil rights movement between 1955 and 1965.

questions.q: What was the name of the 1963 Birmingham campaign plan, named after the 'C' for confrontation?

questions.q: What document did King write while jailed in April 1963, defending direct non-violent action?

questions.q: What was the 'Children's Crusade' of May 1963?
options: Young people marching in Birmingham, many of whom were arrested
A voter registration drive in Mississippi
A boycott of lunch counters in Greensboro

questions.q: Evaluate the claim that Martin Luther King was the most important factor in the success of the civil rights movement between 1954 and 1965.

questions.q: To what extent was the Civil Rights Act of 1964 a turning point for African Americans?

math-hl.topic: Paper 3 skills: extended problem-solving and investigation

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Paper 3 often asks you to 'conjecture' a result. What is a conjecture?
options: A statement believed true from evidence but not yet proved
questions.answer: A statement believed true from evidence but not yet proved
questions.hint: It comes after spotting a pattern.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the sum of the first 10 odd positive integers.
questions.hint: Add 1, 3, 5, … and compare with square numbers.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The sums 1, 1+3, 1+3+5, … give 1, 4, 9, … Conjecture a formula for the sum of the first n odd numbers, in terms of n.
questions.hint: Compare each total with the number of terms used.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the value of 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³ + 5³.
questions.hint: Compare your answer with (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5)².

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which formula gives 1³ + 2³ + … + n³?
questions.hint: Test your options with n = 2, where the sum is 9.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A convex polygon with n sides has n(n − 3)/2 diagonals. How many diagonals does a decagon have?
questions.hint: A decagon has 10 sides.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Someone conjectures that n² + n + 41 is prime for every positive integer n. Find the smallest positive integer n that is a counterexample.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: In a proof by mathematical induction, what must be shown after the basis case?
options: If the result holds for n = k, then it holds for n = k + 1
The result holds for n = 2 and n = 3
The result holds for all negative n
questions.answer: If the result holds for n = k, then it holds for n = k + 1
questions.hint: This step lets the result 'pass along' from one integer to the next.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Which single example is enough to disprove 'for all real x, x² > x'?
questions.hint: Look at numbers between 0 and 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Let u₁ = 1, u₂ = 1 and uₙ₊₂ = uₙ₊₁ + uₙ. Find u₁ + u₂ + … + u₈.
questions.hint: Write out the terms up to u₁₀ and compare the sum with u₁₀.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: For the sequence above, the sum of the first n terms equals u_(n+k) − 1. Find k.
questions.hint: Use your previous answer: which term is 55?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: How many regions are formed inside a circle when 4 points on it are all joined by chords, with no three chords meeting at one point?
questions.hint: Count carefully: 1, 2, 4 regions for 1, 2, 3 points.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The region counts for 1 to 5 points are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. What does a Paper 3 investigation show for 6 points?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the number of ways to choose 2 objects from 8, which is also the number of handshakes among 8 people who each shake hands once.

questions.q: Prove by induction that 1 + 3 + 5 + … + (2n − 1) = n² for all positive integers n.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain why checking a conjecture for the first 1000 values of n does not prove it, and describe what a full proof requires.
questions.hint: Think about the counterexample at n = 40 for n² + n + 41.

math-sl.topic: Paper 2 skills: GDC strategies for functions and statistics

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use your GDC to solve e^x = x + 2 for x > 0. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.q: Use your GDC to find the negative solution of e^x = x + 2, to 3 significant figures.

questions.q: Use your GDC to find the smallest root of x³ − 4x + 1 = 0, to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Zoom out to see all three zeros.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: For the data 12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 30, find the mean.

questions.q: For x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2.1, 3.9, 6.2, 7.8, 10.1, find the gradient of the regression line of y on x, to 3 significant figures.

questions.q: X ~ N(50, 4²). Find k such that P(X < k) = 0.9, to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use the inverse normal function.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: X ~ B(10, 0.2). Find P(X = 3), to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use the binomial probability density function.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: X ~ B(10, 0.2). Find P(X ≥ 3), to 3 significant figures.
questions.hint: Use 1 − P(X ≤ 2).

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A GDC shows an intersection at x = 1.146193. How should you write it in a Paper 2 answer unless told otherwise?
questions.hint: IB answers are exact or correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain when it is better to solve an equation algebraically rather than with a GDC in Paper 2, and what you must write so the examiner can follow GDC work.
questions.hint: Think about exact answers, 'show that' questions, and naming the GDC function used.

questions.hint: Take logs of both sides.

questions.q: A graph of a measured quantity against an independent variable is a straight line that does not pass through the origin when theory says it should. What does this most likely suggest?

questions.hint: This kind of error shifts every reading by the same amount.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: How do error bars help when drawing a line of best fit?
options: A good line should pass through all or nearly all error bars
The line must go through every data point exactly
They show which points to delete
questions.answer: A good line should pass through all or nearly all error bars
questions.hint: Think about what the bars represent.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: How is the uncertainty in a gradient usually estimated in IB practical work?

From the number of data points

questions.hint: Draw lines of maximum and minimum gradient.

questions.q: Which change reduces random error in timing oscillations?

Using a stopwatch with a zero error

questions.q: A force–extension graph is linear up to 12 N at an extension of 0.040 m. Find the spring constant in N m⁻¹.
questions.hint: Use the gradient F/x.

questions.q: In an experiment to find the specific heat capacity of a metal, the value obtained is lower than the accepted value. Suggest a reason and an improvement.

questions.q: Explain the difference between accuracy and precision, using a set of repeated measurements as an example.

A ruler with a worn end
A balance that reads 0.2 g with nothing on it
A thermometer that always reads 1 °C too high
questions.answer: Variation in reaction time when using a stopwatch
questions.hint: Random errors scatter readings above and below the true value.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the usual uncertainty of a reading on an analogue ruler with 1 mm divisions?
questions.hint: Many teachers use half the smallest division.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A mass is 50.0 ± 0.5 g. Find the percentage uncertainty.

questions.q: Two lengths 12.0 ± 0.2 cm and 8.0 ± 0.1 cm are added. Find the absolute uncertainty of the total, in cm.

questions.hint: Speed is the gradient.

It reduces the number of variables

As many as the calculator shows

psych-hl.topic: Concepts in applied psychology: responsibility and ethics

questions.q: In applied psychology, what does 'responsibility' mainly refer to?

The obligation to publish only positive results
The need to use only lab experiments

questions.hint: Think about who could be affected by research and its use.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which APA ethical principle concerns benefiting people and avoiding harm?

questions.q: What is the term for the process of fully explaining a study to participants after it ends, especially when deception was used?

questions.q: Why is informed consent particularly complex in research with children?

Consent is only needed for adults over 65

questions.hint: Consider who can legally and cognitively agree.

questions.subject: psych

The results took a long time to analyse

questions.hint: Consider the wider impact on society.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an ethics committee (review board)?
options: To weigh the costs and benefits of proposed research before it begins
questions.answer: To weigh the costs and benefits of proposed research before it begins
questions.hint: It acts before the study starts.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: In a covert observation in a workplace, which ethical issue is most obvious?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which practice protects participants' identity when reporting case studies?
options: Using pseudonyms or initials and removing identifying details
questions.answer: Using pseudonyms or initials and removing identifying details
questions.hint: Think about anonymity.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: What term describes participants' right to leave a study at any time, including removing their data?
questions.hint: It applies even after the study has started.

questions.q: Why can deception sometimes be justified in social psychology research?

It is required by all ethics codes
It removes the need for consent forms entirely

questions.subject: psych

Confidentiality means data is published openly

Animals being too similar to humans

So the therapist can charge more
questions.answer: So the client can make an informed choice
questions.hint: This links to consent.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which word describes giving participants a false impression about the aim of a study?

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Why might researchers use a pilot study when designing research on a sensitive topic?

questions.answer: To spot problems, including ethical risks, before the main study
questions.hint: It is a small trial run.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which right means a participant can leave a study whenever they want?
